D2.why: The top three stop-doing items are 'Stop chasing 800 stores and $15B' and 'Stop funding ventures outside electronics', and the register warns against stage 4 salvation moves; but it also pushes full separation and eventual spin-off of the used-car business, which the key says should have been kept, and redesigns commission pay.

D3.why: The most urgent brutal fact is that Rival B 'has led on sales, earnings, profit per store and national share for about four years', rated Critical with its consequence stated; the register also lists the venture losses, the appliance price attack, the unvalidated commission model and the ageing store base.

D5.why: Gate 10 marks stage 1 hubris ('great shape'), stage 2 ventures and targets, and stage 3 denial as present, then names stage 4 ('new CEO copies Rival B wholesale… dramatic program launched before test results') and stage 5 (buybacks, ageing stores, counselors leaving), each with a fitting early warning sign.

D7.why: Derived figures (about $2.0B used-car revenue, $198.5M disc losses, 19% growth needed for $15B, about $18.6M sales per store) check out against the dossier and are labelled as derived; assumptions are tagged, and missing ROE, profit per store, satisfaction and remodel cost are flagged as able to overturn the hedgehog.

D8.why: The opening verdict gives the hedgehog sentence, weakest flywheel link, top three stop-doing items, most urgent brutal fact and missing numbers, and is actionable, but with the score rationale and evidence note it runs past one phone screen.
